symptom: `revoke create, delete, write * on entity M.E from M.Admin` refused with `the access rule on E for Customer, SupportAgent, Admin also grants Customer, SupportAgent, which this revoke does not name` on every run, though that shared rule granted only `read *` and the revoke would not change it
cause: RevokeEntityMemberAccess refused any rule holding a named role together with an unnamed one (#1501's guard) before asking whether the revocation would modify that rule
fix: narrowAccessRule computes the change with a dry-run flag; a shared rule is refused only if the dry run reports a change, otherwise skipped. The same function applies the narrowing to the target rules, so the check and the write cannot disagree
insight: A guard against a side effect must be conditioned on the side effect actually happening: #1501 refused 'a rule I would narrow for unnamed roles', but tested only role membership, not narrowing. Typical trigger is an additive `grant read * … to A, B, Admin` next to an Admin-only CRUD rule — the shared rule exists precisely because it grants less
